takeaways: Weil Gotshal's planned dissolution puts ~400K sf at the GM Building at risk ahead of a $1.6B SASB maturing next June; refinancing near 6% could add ~$58M a year of debt service (via The Promote).
Lenders are tightening even for AI's biggest names (Broadcom had to add guarantees to save a $63B Anthropic chip-lease deal) while PE faces a ~$300B debt wall.
Opportunistic capital keeps flowing into senior housing and CRE: Town Lane's $1.9B fund (with a senior housing platform), Apollo's Mubadala Capital stake, and Blackstone's $1.5B MarineMax deal.

items.headline: Weil Gotshal plans to dissolve, leaving BXP a ~400K sf hole at the GM Building
items.summary: Weil holds about 400K sf through 2034 at rents in the $140s/sf versus $200s/sf market. The tower's $2.3B 2017 CMBS (about $1.6B SASB at 3.6%) matures next June, and BXP's CFO expects refinancing near 6%, roughly $138M a year versus about $80M today. SL Green's Green Loan is special servicer if it goes distressed (via The Promote, WSJ).

items.headline: Town Lane, Blackstone alum, raises $1.9B fund in five months, including a senior housing platform
items.summary: Tyler Henritze's firm topped its $1.25B debut fund and says it is playing offense amid dislocation. Deals include a Midtown Atlanta office tower, a 2.7M sf industrial portfolio and senior housing platform Arcole. Fresh opportunistic capital is targeting senior housing (via The Promote).

items.headline: Private-equity-backed companies face a $300B debt wall
items.summary: Roughly $300B of portfolio-company maturities are looming as lenders tighten terms, a read-through for any operator or sponsor refinancing in the next 24 months (via WSJ 10-Point).

items.headline: Fannie and Freddie may issue new multifamily lending licenses early next year
items.summary: These would be the first new agency licenses since Basis Investment Group in 2022. Freddie wants a cut when licenses trade, including in the Bayview/Morgan family purchase of a majority stake in BWE (via The Promote).

items.headline: Apollo buys nearly 10% of Mubadala Capital, majority owner of Fortress
items.summary: The stake extends Apollo into mezz/pref and CWCapital special servicing, adding to Athene and Atlas warehouse lending. Mubadala is a $385B sovereign wealth fund (via The Promote).

items.headline: Broadcom CEO steps in to save $63B Anthropic chip-lease debt deal as banks demand better terms
items.summary: Banks spooked by rising rates and AI overexposure wanted better terms before committing $42B. Hock Tan conceded higher interest and guarantees covering an Anthropic default, a sign lenders are raising the bar even for AI's largest players (via WSJ 10-Point).

items.headline: Weil Gotshal leaders move to wind down one of the industry's most venerable law firms
items.summary: Weil lost top lawyers, had no succession plan after the incoming chair declined, and consulted a bankruptcy lawyer. A lesson in how fast talent flight compounds once confidence breaks (via WSJ 10-Point).

items.headline: Senior living dealbook: 1019 Senior Living buys two AL communities (150 units); seven-community portfolio trades
items.summary: 1019 now operates eight communities across Indiana and Ohio, and Ciel Senior Living took over management of Sopris Lodge in Carbondale, CO, its sixth Colorado community. Regional operator consolidation continues.

items.headline: Blackstone's Safe Harbor to buy MarineMax for $1.5B cash at $53/share, a 96% premium
items.summary: The all-cash deal (announced Aug 10) follows a competitive strategic review and is expected to close before year-end, pending shareholder and regulatory approval. MarineMax has ~70 dealerships and 65 marina/storage sites, and fiscal Q3 revenue fell 7% to $611.3M even as gross margin rose to 35.7%. Infrastructure capital is paying up for recurring-revenue marinas while boat retail stays weak.

items.headline: Trian group bids $7.35/share to take Wendy's private
items.summary: Nelson Peltz's Trian, the largest shareholder, is part of the cash offer, but the stock traded at that level just last month. Another take-private test of public-market valuations (via WSJ 10-Point).

items.headline: Bushburg buys Barnett's 259 Clinton site for about $100M; Dushinsky joins Chetrit's Two Bridges site
items.summary: The sites allow over 2,700 units, and Bushburg can build about 600K sf of residential. Chetrit defaulted on a small Madison Realty mezz loan at 265-275 Cherry (via The Promote).

items.headline: Tishman Speyer lands Bouwinvest for new office vehicle, starting with the Chrysler Building
items.summary: SASBs lead CMBS conduits 3:1, and BGO is rebranding back to GreenOak. Pensford put a December Fed hike at 80% likely (via The Promote).

items.headline: 186,000 adjustable-rate mortgages reset next year with big payment jumps
items.summary: The largest group is 2020 seven-year ARMs facing a median increase of nearly $1,300 a month, a household-finance squeeze that touches adult children of residents and move-in decisions (via WSJ 10-Point).

items.headline: AI quintuples flash-memory prices, ending Apple's supplier leverage
items.summary: Apple will spend about $25B on flash this year versus $6B in 2025 for roughly the same volume. Tim Cook called rising memory prices a '100-year flood' (via WSJ 10-Point).

items.headline: JetBlue hits record low after creditors reportedly hire restructuring advisers
items.summary: High jet fuel prices pressure the turnaround, though earnings contained encouraging liquidity news (via WSJ 10-Point).

items.headline: 50% aluminum tariff sends U.S. prices to a record premium
items.summary: The U.S. relies on Canadian aluminum, and the tariff is hurting automakers, tech developers and home buyers, with construction-cost implications (via WSJ 10-Point).

items.headline: Senior housing supply growth at record low: 0.7% inventory growth, 29-month construction cycles
items.summary: NIC MAP data (Q3 2025) put occupancy at 88.7%, with IL at 90.2% and AL at 87.2%. Projects starting in early 2026 are unlikely to open before 2028, so occupancy gains and rent growth (3-6% expected) should persist for existing operators.

items.headline: BizBuySell Q3: 2,132 small businesses sold, median price $350K (+17% YoY)
items.summary: Closed deals were down 7% YoY, but median cash flow rose 5% to $156K. Deals above $1M averaged 3.73x cash flow and sold at 100.8% of ask, versus 2.30x and 93.6% below $1M. Service businesses were 47% of deals; restaurants fell 23%. New SBA rules took effect Oct 1.

items.headline: Acquisition entrepreneurship goes mainstream as owners retire
items.summary: A 2026 JPMorgan Chase survey found 40% of small business owners plan to retire within a decade, and about 70% have no formal or only early succession plans. Search funds, SBA loans and personal capital are financing buyers, with HVAC, accounting, home services and B2B services the common targets. Founder dependency is the key diligence risk (Forbes, May 2026).

items.headline: JPMorgan's 270 Park Avenue HQ estimated to cost about $6B
items.summary: The estimate is the bank's internal real-estate figure for the tallest occupied office building in the U.S., which it has never officially disclosed (via WSJ 10-Point).

items.headline: Anthropic's implied $40 trillion market opportunity ahead of its IPO
items.summary: The figure is based on the global economic value of knowledge-worker output (via WSJ 10-Point).

items.headline: China's EV makers run out of domestic buyers as zombie brands persist
items.summary: China passenger-car sales are down 22% through September, on track for the worst year since 2014, pushing overcapacity into exports (via WSJ 10-Point).

items.headline: Microsoft and Skydance use voluntary buyouts to shrink headcount
items.summary: Voluntary exits are a softer route to workforce reductions (via WSJ 10-Point).

items.headline: Hiten Samtani grades The Promote Insider's first year a B+
items.summary: Planned fixes include a host migration, new contributors and podcast transcripts; the first live podcast event is Nov 5 in Lower Manhattan (via The Promote).

items.headline: 'Buy, borrow, die' securities-backed lending reaches $5.4T globally
items.summary: Per Deloitte, portfolio-backed lending is spreading below the billionaire tier (via WSJ 10-Point).

items.headline: Mystery buyer pays $311M for 19-acre Naples beachfront compound
items.summary: Assembled via two deals ($225M and $86M) behind a land trust and NDAs (via WSJ 10-Point).

items.headline: MarineMax deal shows what buyers value: marinas, service and superyacht over boat retail
items.summary: Safe Harbor, the largest US marina and superyacht service business (bought by Blackstone for $5.65B in April 2025), gets waterfront sites that are scarce and generate recurring fleet revenue. Combined, it could offer purchase, financing, berthing, maintenance, charter and resale under one roof.
